title: Mr. Malone
paragraphs: Crime drama based on Craig Rice's lawyer-detective John J. Malone, who solves murders and other mysteries through investigation rather than courtroom procedure.

Crime drama centered on Chicago criminal attorney John J. Malone, created by novelist Craig Rice. Frozen GRH subset spans four title/cast/network eras from 1947 through the complete May-July 1951 NBC run.

GRH documents the program through Murder and Mr. Malone / Lovejoy (January 11, 1947 to April 10, 1948) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], The Amazing Mr. Malone / Lovejoy (April 24, 1948 to March 26, 1949) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], The Amazing Mr. Malone / Gene Raymond (September 21, 1949 to September 24, 1950) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], and The Amazing Mr. Malone / George Petrie (May 25, 1951 to July 13, 1951) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Bernard L. Schubert (producer on 12 recordings and transcriber on 1 recording), Craig Rice (creator on 12 recordings), Eugene Wang (writer on 11 recordings), George Petrie (performer on 8 recordings), Larry Haines (performer on 7 recordings), Richard Lewis (director on 7 recordings), and Fred Collins (announcer on 6 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Chicago crime and legal world, Craig Rice literary character continuity, criminal defense lawyer investigation, murder investigation, proverb and cliché case-title structure, and network radio crime-drama transition.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Postwar American radio crime and legal drama, 1951 NBC final run, 1948 title change to The Amazing Mr. Malone, and John J. Malone radio actor succession.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]] (4 shared credited people), [[show|pat-novak-for-hire|Pat Novak, for Hire]] (6 shared credited people), [[show|cbs-radio-workshop|CBS Radio Workshop]] (3 shared credited people), [[show|escape|Escape]] (4 shared credited people), and [[show|molle-mystery-theatre|Molle Mystery Theatre]] (5 shared credited people).
